tasks.notes: check_provenance.py has no plan-level twin of the task-level "defense in depth" guard. A task Claim carrying an unrecognizable tag draws `provenance: task <id> claim carries no recognizable provenance tag …` (check_provenance.py:120-128), but a header Claim whose tag this grammar does not know — `**Claim:** … (derived)`, or a tag wrapped past recognition — makes `plan_claim_provenance` return None, so `plan_provenance` is "" and the header is skipped silently by the layer that runs FIRST. The compiler's `plan_claim_violations` is still the second wall (and M2 pins that it refuses), so nothing this task's Machine clauses require is unmet; the asymmetry is only against the file's own stated doctrine ("the first layer must not bless what it cannot classify"). If you want the symmetry, add, beside the header block at check_provenance.py:98: `elif _plan_claim_raw-ish presence and not plan_provenance: failures.append("provenance: plan-level claim carries no recognizable provenance tag — `(elicited)` or `(quoted from #NNN)`")` — which needs `parse_plan_claim(md_text) is not None` as the presence test.; The plan-level empty-sentence guard (check_provenance.py:107-113, `provenance: plan-level claim quotes #N with an empty operator sentence …`) is added code that no test in tests/test_check_provenance.py exercises: delete that `elif not sentence:` branch and the exam stays green (a header that is nothing but `(quoted from #1)` folds to "", which is a substring of every body, so it would then pass vacuously). Its task-level twin is pinned by test_claim_that_is_only_its_provenance_tag_refuses:223. No Machine clause names this row — M4 names only the not-verbatim and does-not-resolve lines — so it is advisory, but a four-line test modelled on the task-level one would close it.; Documentation drift inside this task's own FILES: tests/test_plan_level_claim.py:3 still opens "A claims-v1 plan carries ONE elicited operator sentence above the first task", which the same file now pins as false — test_755_a_quoted_header_claim_earns_no_grammar_violation:437 accepts a header signed `(quoted from #1)`. The module docstring should say "elicited or quoted from an issue", matching the SKILL.md §The document and §Self-review rewordings the diff already makes.; Duplicated logic: the new plan-level block in `skills/ultrawrite/scripts/check_provenance.py` (lines ~96-116 of the patched file) reproduces the task-level quote-resolution structure verbatim — same `issue_body(number, gh, cache)` fetch, same `fold(...)` comparison, same three branches (unresolvable / empty sentence / not verbatim) — differing only in the failure-line subject (`plan-level claim` vs `task %s claim`). A future change to the matching rule (a different fold, a new branch) has to be made in two places. Extract one helper used by both, e.g. `def _resolve_quote(subject, number, sentence, gh, cache) -> list[str]` returning the failure lines with `subject` interpolated (`"plan-level claim"` / `"task %s claim" % task["id"]`), and call it from the header block and from the task loop. Behavior-preserving: the four existing task-level pins in `tests/test_check_provenance.py` and the four new `#755 Task 1` pins keep the exact line strings.; Uncovered branch: the plan-level `provenance: plan-level claim quotes #%s with an empty operator sentence — the Claim is nothing but its provenance tag` failure in `skills/ultrawrite/scripts/check_provenance.py` has no leg in the exam. M4 names only the not-verbatim and does-not-resolve lines, so this is not a missing criterion — but the branch is a real guard (check_provenance runs ahead of the compiler that refuses a tag-only header, and without it `""` is a substring of every body, so a header quoting nothing would pass), and deleting it today leaves both `tests/test_check_provenance.py` and `tests/test_plan_level_claim.py` green. One row under the `#755 Task 1` comment closes it: `_plan_with_header(tmp_path, "(quoted from #1)", _task("1", TASK_SENTENCE + " (elicited)", SPEC_ANCHOR))` against `_fake_gh(tmp_path, {"1": ISSUE_1})`, asserting exit 2 and that stdout line — the plan-level twin of the existing task-level vacuous-pass pin.

`_test_paths_in_order` (compile_plan.py, new block after the sha-unguarded registration) reimplements path extraction from a Files bullet with `PATH_RE.findall(rest)` + a manual `p.split(":")[0]`, where the compiler already has `_claims_file_paths(value)` (compile_plan.py:422) doing exactly that — backticked path-like tokens, else the first token when it is path-like, `:line-range` stripped — and already used by `proof_tests_ordered` for the same document-order-deduped shape. Two consequences beyond the duplication: (1) the render silently misses a legal but unbackticked Files bullet (`- Test: tests/foo.py`), which `_files_violations` explicitly declines to flag (compile_plan.py:1698-1701) and which the legacy Files parser still folds into `t["reads"]` via its first-token fallback (compile_plan.py:1355-1362) — so for such a plan M1's "each of its `Test:` paths" draws nothing; (2) it skips the `_is_pathlike` filter, so a backticked non-path token in a Test bullet is only kept out by the `accepted` re-filter rather than by the same rule everything else uses. The exam cannot catch either: `_exam_task` backticks every path. Fix is one line, and the `accepted` re-filter still keeps the result a subset of `reads`.; unverified: acceptance is `suite`, but the evidence here is this task's own exam only (`tests/test_compile_plan_base_sha_in_suite.py`, 25 passed) plus the three constraint checks. The new render fires on every `--renders` run, so the global constraint that no other `--renders` consumer changes is not settled by this diff. Two things I could check statically and that hold: no fixture plan under `tests/fixtures/plans/` names any of the five BASE suites the task's Context lists as carrying a repository commit sha, nor either token-reading suite, under `Test:` — so no corpus plan gains a base-sha-in-suite line; and the bare-`--check` path never reaches `ADVISORY_RENDERS` (`render_advisories`, compile_plan.py:2563, is the only consumer), so the Run-less byte-pin is structurally safe. What would settle the rest is a full `python3 -m pytest -q tests` plus the fleet suite on this tree — in particular `tests/test_check_renders.py`, `tests/test_check_renders_pin_is_tree_independent.py`, `tests/test_compile_plan_proof_species.py` and `tests/test_compile_plan_proof_tests.py`, the four that read `--renders` output over shared fixtures.; M1 says the render reads "each of its `Test:` paths that is a tracked file of the checkout", but `_test_paths_in_order` (compile_plan.py, new block) collects paths only from `PATH_RE.findall(rest)` — backticked tokens. BASE's Files parser also admits an unbackticked first token (compile_plan.py:1354-1362, the `- Test: tests/foo.py — the suite` shape), so such a path lands in `task["reads"]` yet never reaches the render: a tracked, unbackticked `Test:` file carrying the token or a resolving sha draws no line. The exam's fixtures backtick every probe (`_exam_task`), so no leg catches it. Narrow and advisory-only — the species' positive legs are all evidenced — hence minor, but the render is silent on a shape the Files parser accepts. The fallback filters back through `accepted`, so it cannot fabricate a path the parser rejected.; plan-defect: M2 and the Context specify the commit test as `_git(base, "cat-file", "-e", sha + "^{commit}")`, claiming it "returns `\"\"` on a miss". It also returns `""` on a hit — `cat-file -e` prints nothing either way and BASE's `_git` (compile_plan.py:2507-2515) returns `p.stdout` on success — so a literal transcription would make the render unconditionally silent and every M2 leg fail. The implementer diverged to `rev-parse --verify --quiet <sha>^{commit}` and disclosed the reason in `_resolves_as_commit`'s docstring; that divergence is correct and lawful, and the exam confirms it (exit 0). Recorded so the operator can correct the plan text rather than the diff — the fix lies in the task's own Machine/Context wording, outside FILES.; The exam's module docstring asserts "only the Proof's `Test:` bullets carry document order, which leg (b) turns on", but the render reads the **Files:** block's `files_raw` pairs, and `_exam_task` emits the probes in the same order in both blocks — so leg (b) cannot in fact discriminate Proof order from Files order. The leg still pins what M1 requires (`Test:` order, not path order, with per-file line numbers), so nothing is left unverified; the comment just misdescribes which view the render consumes and would mislead the next editor of this file. Reword it to say the Files block's verbatim `(label, rest)` pairs are what carry the order.
